Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:10:1.hebrew: ופליג עליה בחדא - דר' שמעון בעי ראשו ורובו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:10:1.english: And disagrees with him in one [matter] - For Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body [to resemble its mother].

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:11:1.hebrew: ואיכא דמקשי - קושיא להך ברייתא, ומתוך הקושיא משיב דבר לשואל אי בעי ר' שמעון ראשו ורובו לאכילה, או לא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:11:1.english: And there are those who raise a difficulty - [They raise] a difficulty against this baraita, and through the difficulty he responds to the questioner [as to] whether Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body for eating, or not.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:11:2.hebrew: מי מיעברא - טהורה מטמא, דקתני: ועבורו מן הטמא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:11:2.english: Can it become pregnant? - [Can] a kosher [animal become pregnant] from a non-kosher [animal], that [the baraita] teaches: “And its impregnation was from the non-kosher [animal]”?

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:13:1.hebrew: חוץ מר' אליעזר ומחלוקתו - שחולקין בכוי בפ' אותו ואת בנו בשחיטת חולין (דף עט:) אם אותו ואת בנו נוהג בו, וקתני: כוי הבא מן התייש ומן הצבייה — אלמא חיה מתעברת מבהמה לדבריהם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:13:1.english: Except for Rabbi Eliezer and his disputants - Who disagree concerning a koy in the chapter [entitled] 'Oto Ve'et Beno' in [tractate] Sheḥitat Ḥullin (79b), whether [the prohibition of] 'it and its offspring' applies to it; and it is taught: A koy that comes from a he-goat and a female gazelle — evidently, an undomesticated animal can become pregnant from a domesticated animal according to their opinion.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:14:1.hebrew: ואמר ר' ירמיה - האי עבורו מן הטמא דקאמר, היינו שנתעברה מן הקלוט — שפרסותיו קלוטות כגמל, ובן פרה הוא — ואליבא דר' שמעון קרי ליה טמא, ובנו מותר אם דומה לאמו בסימן אחד. אלמא, לאכילה לא בעי ר"ש ראשו ורובו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:14:1.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya says - This [phrase], "its pregnancy from an impure [animal]," that it stated, means that it became pregnant from an animal with closed hooves whose hooves are closed like a camel's, and it is the offspring of a cow; and in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Shimon, [the baraita] calls it "impure." And its offspring is permitted if it resembles its mother in one characteristic. Evidently, for consumption, Rabbi Shimon does not require its head and the majority of its body.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:16:1.hebrew: זה וזה גורם - ההיתר והאיסור גורמין לזה שיבא — הוא טמא, ואמו טהורה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:16:1.english: [Both] this and that cause [it] - The permitted [factor] and the forbidden [factor] cause this [offspring] to come [into being] — he [the sire] is non-kosher, and its mother is kosher.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:17:1.hebrew: ולד טריפה - ואביו תמים, הרי זה וזה גורם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:17:1.english: The offspring of a tereifa - And its father is unblemished, [so] behold, [both] this and that cause [it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:18:1.hebrew: דא"כ - דעבורו מן הטמא אסור, לכתוב: "שה כשבים ועזים":
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:18:1.english: For if so - That its conception from a non-kosher [animal] is forbidden, let [the verse] write: "A sheep of sheep and goats."

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:1:1.english: It is different from a camel - In that it resembles its mother in some of its characteristics:

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:23:1.english: Water enters, water exits, and [the fact] that it is turbid is the heat of the flesh - Due to the heat and stench of the flesh.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:24:1.hebrew: מטמא - הוי משמע מגופיה דטמא. ״מן הטמא״ משמע מינו של טמא — הן דדמו לחלב:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:24:1.english: From a non-kosher [animal] - [This] would imply [something that emerges] from the body of the non-kosher [animal] itself. “From the non-kosher” implies a type of non-kosher [substance] — [namely,] those [fluids] that resemble milk.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:2:1.hebrew: אסור באכילה - ומאן שמעת ליה הך סברא? ר"ש. ואם ראשו ורובו כו' — וקס"ד דמדקתני להו בהדי הדדי, ש"מ דאפי' לאכילה בעי ר"ש ראשו ורובו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:2:1.english: Is forbidden for consumption - And whom have you heard [who holds] this reasoning? Rabbi Shimon. "And if its head and the majority of it, etc." — and it entered [the Gemara's] mind that since it taught them together, learn from it that even for consumption Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:3:1.hebrew: מדשבקה לאכילה - דאיירי ברישא, וקם ליה אבכורה, ולא אמר "אם ראשו ורובו דומה לאמו מותר באכילה" — ש"מ: לאכילה סגי במקצת סימנין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:3:1.english: Since he left [the topic of] consumption - For he was dealing [with it] in the first clause, yet he turned to [the status of] a firstborn and did not say, "If its head and the majority of it resemble its mother, it is permitted for consumption" — learn from this: for consumption, some of the signs suffice.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:4:1.english: It was necessary regarding firstborn status - And actually, in both [cases] we require its head and the majority of its [body].

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:5:1.hebrew: זה אי אתה אוכל - גמל, אפי' נולד מן הפרה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:5:1.english: This you may not eat - A camel, even if it was born from a cow.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:5:2.hebrew: אבל אתה אוכל אחר הבא בסימן אחד - של אמו, כלומר שדומה לאמו במקצת, כגון טמא שנולד מן הטהור ודומה לאמו במקצת:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:5:2.english: But you may eat another that comes with one sign - [A sign] of its mother; that is to say, that it resembles its mother somewhat, such as a non-kosher [animal] that was born from a kosher [animal] and resembles its mother somewhat.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:7:1.english: A sheep of sheep - A sheep that comes from two sheep.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:8:1.hebrew: להתיר את המותר - דכיון דאביו ואמו טהורים, לא איצטריך האי קרא דאך את זה תאכלו למישרייה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:8:1.english: To permit that which is permitted - For since its father and its mother are kosher, this verse of “Nevertheless these shall you eat” was not needed to permit it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:8:2.hebrew: מ"מ - מדכתיב "שה" "שה" תרי זימני, שמע מיניה דאפי' מצד האם, ולא מצד האב:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:8:2.english: In any case - Since it is written "a sheep," "a sheep" twice, learn from it that even from the mother's side and not from the father's side:

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:9:1.english: Refers to it as non-kosher - To a solid-hoofed animal [kalut] that was born from a kosher [animal].

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:9:2.hebrew: כר"ש - דאסר ליה היכא דאין בו מקצת סימנין, וקאמר דאם יש לו סימן אחד של טהרה, שדומה לאמו במקצת — מותר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:9:2.english: In accordance with Rabbi Shimon - Who forbids it where it does not have some [kosher] signs; and [the tanna] says that if it has one sign of purity, such that it resembles its mother partially, [it is] permitted.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:13:1.hebrew: חוץ מדרבי אליעזר ומחלוקתו - הא דלא קאמר: "חוץ מן הדולפנין שפרים ורבים מבני אדם", כדאמר לקמן — לא קשה מידי; דלא איירי רבי יהושע בן לוי אלא בבהמה וחיה, ולא בבני אדם, והנהו בני ימא נינהו:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:13:1.english: "Except for Rabbi Eliezer and his disputants" - That which [the Gemara] did not state: "Except for the dolphins, which reproduce from human beings," as it states below — is not difficult at all; for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi was dealing only with domesticated and undomesticated animals, and not with human beings, and those are creatures of the sea.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:15:1.hebrew: ופליג עליה בחדא - מה שיוכל לדחות דחי כן, משום דבמסקנא לאכילה פשטינן נמי דבעי ר"ש ראשו ורובו:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:15:1.english: "And disagrees with him with regard to one" - Whatever [the Gemara] can deflect, it deflects in this manner, because in the conclusion, we resolve that with regard to consumption as well, Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:17:1.hebrew: והא איפכא שמעינן להו ולד טריפה - למ"ד טריפה יולדת, ניחא דפליגי בזה וזה גורם; אלא למ"ד אינה יולדת, מוקמי פלוגתא פרק אלו טריפות (חולין נח.) בעובר ירך אמו, ונתעברה ולבסוף נטרפה. ומיהו אשכחן בעלמא דר' אליעזר סבר זה וזה גורם אסור, ורבנן סברי מותר — גבי שאור חולין ותרומה, ושלהי כל הצלמים (ע"ז מט.) גבי נטל ממנה עצים; אלא לרבי יהושע אייתיה, ואע"ג דלאו דברי הכל הוא. ומה שמזכיר כאן זה וזה גורם, ופר' אותו ואת בנו (חולין עט:) נקט לישנא דחוששין לזרע האב — משום דהכא איירי בדבר הבא מהיתר ואיסור, [שייך שפיר] זה וזה גורם. ומיהו קשה: כיון דאין חוששין לזרע האב, מאיזה טעם תחשב ולד טריפה זה וזה גורם? לא יחשב שאור גורם, וליתסר:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:17:1.english: "But we have heard them [saying] the opposite: The offspring of a tereifa" - According to the one who says that a tereifa can give birth, it is understandable that they disagree over [the principle of] "this and that cause [it]" [zeh vazeh gorem]; but according to the one who says that [a tereifa] cannot give birth, we establish their dispute in chapter "Elu Tereifot" (Chullin 58a) [as being] regarding [whether] a fetus is [considered] the thigh of its mother, and [in a case where] she conceived [while kosher] and was ultimately rendered a tereifa. However, we find elsewhere that Rabbi Eliezer holds [that when] both this and that cause [it], it is forbidden, and the Rabbis hold [it is] permitted — regarding leaven of non-sacred produce [chullin] and of terumah, and at the end of [the chapter entitled] "Kol HaTzelamim" (Avodah Zarah 49a) regarding [one who] took wood from it [an asherah]; rather, [the Gemara] brought it [i.e., the case of the offspring of a tereifa] on account of Rabbi Yehoshua, even though it is not unanimous [that this dispute concerns "this and that cause it"]. And as for [the Gemara] mentioning "this and that cause [it]" here, whereas in chapter "Oto Ve-et Beno" (Chullin 79b) it used the formulation "one is concerned for the seed of the father" — [this is] because here it is dealing with something that comes from [a mixture of] permitted and forbidden [elements], [so the concept of] "this and that cause [it]" is well-suited. However, this is difficult: Since [it is held that] one is not concerned for the seed of the father, for what reason would the offspring of a tereifa be considered [a case where] both this and that cause [it]? Should it not be considered [as if only] the leaven [of prohibition] caused [it] [i.e., as having only a single, forbidden cause], and let it be forbidden?

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:2:1.hebrew: שמע מינה לאכילה נמי בעי ר"ש ראשו ורובו - דמשמע שאין בו כי אם שני חלוקין, מדלא קתני חלוק שלישי, ולימא: "אם יש בו מקצת סימנין — מותר באכילה", והדר ליתני: "ואם ראשו ורובו דומה לאמו — חייב בבכורה". והשתא, רישא וסיפא רבותא קמשמע לן: דרישא קתני שילדה מין טמאה — דאסור אף באכילה, וסיפא, דקתני ראשו ורובו דומים לאמו — חייב אף בבכורה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:2:1.english: "Learn from it that for consumption as well, Rabbi Shimon requires its head and majority" - For [the wording] implies that there are only two categories [in the baraita], since it does not teach a third category and say: "If it has partial signs, it is permitted for consumption," and then go on to teach: "And if its head and the majority of it resemble its mother, it is obligated in [the law of] the firstborn." And now [that it teaches only these two cases], the first clause and the last clause teach us a novel point: for the first clause teaches that [if] it gave birth to [an offspring of] a non-kosher species, it is forbidden even for consumption; and the last clause teaches that [if] its head and the majority of it resemble its mother, it is obligated even in [the law of] the firstborn.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:5:1.hebrew: זה אי אתה אוכל - גמל ושפן כתיבי בקרא. "אבל אתה אוכל הבא בסימן אחד" — לאו בסימני טהרה איירי, דממעלה גרה וממפריסי הפרסה; אלא בדמי למקצת סימנין לאמו: ביד, וברגל, ובצמרו. (ולד) סימני טהרה בעי:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:5:1.english: "These you may not eat" - The camel and the hyrax are written in the verse. [As for the statement,] "but you may eat [an animal] that comes with one sign" — this is not dealing with signs of kosher status, [such as] chewing the cud and splitting the hoof; rather, [it refers to a case] where it resembles its mother in some characteristics: in the foreleg, in the hind leg, or in its wool. [For does the] offspring require signs of kosher status?

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:7:1.hebrew: עד שיהא אביו ואמו כבשה - מדכתיב "כבשים" ו"עזים" ולא כתיב "כבש" ו"עז", דרש ר' יהושע; ור' אליעזר — מדכתיב "שה" "שה" תרי זימני. והשתא, דרשות דר' יהושע לאסור — לאו הוא דר"א להתיר?! ולשון "לא בא הכתוב" דאמר ר"א מגומגם קצת, דמשמע הלשון דמקרא זה שדרש ר' יהושע טמא שנולד מן טהור ועיבורו מן הטהור, אמר ר"א דבא להוסיף על המותר ולהתיר טמא הנולד מן הטהור ועיבורו מן הטמא. ויש לפרש: "לא בא הכתוב" — כמו "לא באתה התורה". עוד י"ל דברי רבי אליעזר, וה"פ: מ"שה שה" נפקא לן עיבורו מן הטהור, לכך אייתר זה להוסיף על המותר ועיבורו מן הטמא:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:7:1.english: "Unless its father is [a lamb] and its mother is a ewe" - From the fact that it is written "sheep [kesavim]" and "goats [izzim]" and it is not written "a sheep [kesev]" and "a goat [ez]," Rabbi Yehoshua expounded [that both parents must be kosher]; and Rabbi Eliezer [expounded] from the fact that it is written "a sheep [seh]," "a sheep [seh]" twice. And now, [since] Rabbi Yehoshua’s derivation is to forbid, is not Rabbi Eliezer’s [derivation] to permit?! And the phrasing "The verse did not come [to permit that which is permitted...]" that Rabbi Eliezer stated is somewhat difficult, for the phrasing implies that [regarding] this verse, which Rabbi Yehoshua expounded [as referring to] a non-kosher [offspring] born from a kosher [animal] and its conception was from a kosher [animal], Rabbi Eliezer said that it comes to add to that which is permitted and to permit a non-kosher [offspring] born from a kosher [animal] and its conception was from a non-kosher [animal]. And one can explain: "The verse did not come" is like [saying] "The Torah did not come." Alternatively, one can explain the statement of Rabbi Eliezer, and this is its explanation: From "a sheep [seh]," "a sheep [seh]" we derive [permission when] its conception was from a kosher [animal]; therefore, this [text] was superfluous to add to that which is permitted, and [permit even when] its conception was from a non-kosher [animal].
